info.title: Loanpoint API
info.description: JSON API for Loanpoint, the equipment lending desk used by Fairmont University Media Services. The desk lends camera, audio, lighting, support and computing kit. The API covers the catalogue, the loan register, the supervisor approvals queue, and the three-step new-loan draft flow. All money values are integer cents; all dates are calendar dates in YYYY-MM-DD form and all instants are ISO 8601 UTC. The desk clock is frozen, so date-dependent values are reproducible.

get.description: Returns the signed-in desk operator, the frozen desk clock, the department and category lists used by the interface, the selectable loan periods, the latest bookable pickup date, and the policy constants behind the pricing and approval rules.
Returns the desk counter tiles and the four work queues: overdue loans (with a live late-fee preview), loans due back today, loans ready for pickup, and loans awaiting supervisor approval.

get.description: Lists the equipment catalogue, sorted by item name. The free-text filter matches the item name, asset tag and description, case-insensitively. Filters are applied after the total count is taken, so `totalCount` is always the size of the whole catalogue and `shownCount` is the size of the filtered list.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text filter matched case-insensitively against item name, asset tag and description. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored; an empty value applies no filter.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Restrict results to one catalogue category. The value `All`, an empty value, or an omitted parameter applies no category filter. A value outside the category list matches nothing.

parameters.name: availableOnly
parameters.description: When `1` or `true`, only items with at least one available unit are returned. Every other value, including `0` and `false`, leaves the filter off.

get.description: Returns one catalogue item with its specification rows and the list of open loans currently holding units of it. Holders are loans whose status is `pending_approval`, `ready` or `out`, sorted by loan identifier.

get.description: Lists loans, newest identifier first. The status filter is applied before the free-text filter. `totalCount` is the size of the whole register; `shownCount` is the size of the filtered list. An unrecognised `status` value falls back to `all`, and the echoed `filters.status` reports the value actually applied.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Restrict results to one loan status. `overdue` selects loans that are `out` and past their due date, which is a derived state rather than a stored status. Any other value falls back to `all`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text filter matched case-insensitively against the loan identifier and the borrower name. Leading and trailing whitespace is ignored; an empty value applies no filter.

post.description: Adds seven calendar days to the due date, rolling a weekend result forward to the following Monday, and increments the extension counter. post.description: Returns the kit to stock, moves the loan to `returned`, records the returned condition, charges any late fee, and settles the deposit. The deposit outcome is `none` when no deposit was held, `released` when the condition is good, and `held` otherwise. Only a loan whose status is `out` can be checked in.

post.description: Starts the three-step new-loan flow by recording the borrower (step 1). The new draft has no items, a default loan period of 3 days, and a default pickup date of the desk date. The borrower email must be a fairmont.edu address and the department must be one of the desk's departments.

get.description: Returns the draft as the new-loan flow sees it, including the live quote and schedule preview once the draft has at least one item, a loan period and a pickup date.

patch.summary: Update one step of a new-loan draft
patch.description: Applies one step of the new-loan flow to the draft. The `step` field selects which step: `borrower` replaces the borrower and purpose (step 1), `schedule` replaces the item lines, loan period and pickup date (step 2). The schedule step checks item structure first and availability last, and requires a pickup date that is a weekday, not in the past, and no more than 14 calendar days after the desk date.

post.summary: Book the loan from a draft
post.description: Step 3 of the new-loan flow. Re-checks the borrower and schedule recorded on the draft, prices the loan, computes the due date, and books it. The new loan starts in `pending_approval` when it needs supervisor approval, otherwise in `ready`. The draft is discarded once the loan exists. Availability is re-checked at the moment of booking, because units can be committed elsewhere while the draft sits open. The request takes no body.

example.message: L-1049 booked and ready for pickup on Tue 17 Mar 2026.
